# Two splits of one transaction both stating `took_the_residual`.
#
# The sale pays a 5.00 bank charge out of what it fetched, so the transaction
# carries two expense-or-income lines: the charge and the exchange difference.
# Neither the arithmetic nor the account can tell them apart — both are in the
# profit and loss, and a residual would resolve to either — so the key is the
# only thing that says which is the difference, and the file states it twice.
#
# Counted, both would go into `realized_gains_fx`: the 100.00 the sale made and
# the 5.00 the bank took, as though the book had realized 105.00 on selling a
# thousand dollars that cost 1,300.00.
#
# It is the same rule `$residual$` already follows, since two residuals cannot
# be resolved, and it holds however the residual is claimed.
#
# `{usd_basis}` is the guid of the purchase's cost basis, read from
# `fx-balances` after the first import.
2026-06-01 open Expenses
	type: "Expense"
	placeholder: #True
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"
2026-06-01 open Expenses:Bank Charges
	type: "Expense"
	commodity.namespace: "CURRENCY"
	commodity.mnemonic: "CAD"

2026-06-01 * "Sell every dollar at 1.40, less a bank charge"
	currency.mnemonic: "CAD"
	Assets:USD Bank -1000.00 USD
		account.commodity.mnemonic: "USD"
		share_price: "13/10"
		value: "-1300.00"
		cost_basis_split_guid: "{usd_basis}"
	Assets:CAD Bank 1395.00 CAD
	Expenses:Bank Charges 5.00 CAD
		took_the_residual: "true"
	Income:FX Gain -100.00 CAD
		took_the_residual: "true"
